About the Role This is a senior individual contributor role on the team that builds and runs HG's data platform: everything between a raw vendor file landing in our lake and a finished dataset arriving in a customer's hands. It includes the transformation stack that turns messy external signals into product-grade company attributes, the matching systems that decide which company a piece of evidence belongs to and the internal applications our analysts use to curate and correct the result. You will be based in Pune, working with engineers at our Pune, US & Brazil locations. Build the quality layer that catches silent failure: contracts at every handoff, freshness and completeness monitoring, and pipelines that quarantine bad data rather than publish it. Improve entity matching and attribution — and make match decisions explainable to the customers who depend on them. Make our release cycle boring. Recurring deliveries should not depend on people watching them. Treat compute cost as a first-class engineering metric across Spark, orchestration, and the serving tier. Deep Spark and Databricks expertise at multi-terabyte scale, including the operational side of lakehouse table formats — merges, compaction, small files, schema evolution. Airflow orchestration (DAGs, operators, sensors) and integration with Spark/Databricks . Proven experience in AWS ecosystems (EC2, S3, EMR). Python/Scala/Java, with real software discipline: testing, CI/CD, code review, infrastructure as code is a plus. Experience in Docker - Kubernetes, Terraform is a plus. Experience in integrating AI first implementations in traditional data engineering setups will greatly help in shaping our future designs. full_description: Product & Technology Intern | GuruCoolA little about us We're GuruCool, an early-stage technology startup building a connected operating system for educational institutions. Analytical skills to use source materials effectively, think critically, identify risks, and recommend actions. Attention to detail with a focus on accuracy and adherence to standards. Excellent communication skills, both written and oral, with an emphasis on building relationships and promoting collaborative goals. What You’ll Do Design & Build with Google ADK: Design, develop, test, and deploy autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents using Google ADK, Vertex AI Agent Builder, and agentic patterns to address key business challenges. Vertex AI Implementation: Leverage Vertex AI capabilities including model training, fine-tuning, vector search, and orchestration to build production-grade AI solutions that integrate seamlessly with enterprise systems. End-to-End Development: Own the end-to-end technical lifecycle of AI projects on Google Cloud Platform, from initial proof-of-concept and prototyping through to production deployment using Vertex AI Pipelines, monitoring with Vertex AI Model Monitoring, and continuous iteration. Google Cloud Integration: Build integrations between AI agents and Google Cloud services including Gemini Enterprise, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, and enterprise data sources to enable intelligent automation across the organization. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with business stakeholders to understand requirements and collaborate closely with QA Specialists and Cloud Engineers to ensure solutions are reliable, scalable, and seamlessly integrated within GCP infrastructure. Responsible AI Implementation: Implement, test, and monitor safeguards for AI agents using Vertex AI's responsible AI tools to mitigate risks, including bias detection, model explainability, compliance monitoring, and operational limits. Ensure solutions are fair, explainable, and robust. Agentic Architecture with ADK: Contribute to the architecture and selection of frameworks, tools, and orchestration logic using Google ADK and Vertex AI to build, manage, and scale multi-agent systems effectively. Prototype Fast, in the Open: Ship a working prototype in days, not quarters. Put it in a real user’s hands early, watch them use it, and iterate on what you observe instead of what was requested. Build MCP Servers and Tool Integrations: Design, build, and maintain Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, connectors, and tool layers that give Claude, Gemini, and other models safe, governed, audited access to Coupa business systems and data. Stay Multi-Model and Pragmatic: Choose the right model, framework, and pattern for each job across Claude, Gemini, and open models. Make cost, latency, and accuracy tradeoffs deliberately instead of defaulting to one vendor. Know When It Isn’t an Agent: Recognize when workflow automation, a scheduled job, a cleaner integration, or simply deleting a step is the faster, cheaper, more durable fix. Reach for the smallest tool that solves the problem. Instrument and Prove Impact: Measure every deployment. Track usage, cycle-time reduction, hours returned, and error and escalation rates, then report results to stakeholders and leadership in business terms, not model metrics. Carry Trust and Governance into the Field: Apply security, privacy, data-handling, and responsible AI guardrails at the point of deployment. Engage Security, Legal, and Data Governance early so solutions clear review the first time. Enable, Document, and Hand Off: Leave behind runbooks, monitoring, and trained business owners so what you build survives without you. Convert one-off wins into reusable patterns, templates, and internal skills the whole AI Delivery team can redeploy. Iterate & Improve: Monitor agent performance in production using Vertex AI monitoring tools, gather feedback, and iteratively improve models, prompts, grounding strategies, and agent logic to drive successful adoption and business impact. Hands-on experience with Google Vertex AI, including model deployment, endpoint management, and AI agent development. Strong knowledge of AI/ML fundamentals, agentic AI patterns (e.g., ReAct, planning, tool use, function calling), and experience with Google ADK or Vertex AI Agent Builder. Proficiency in Python and Google Cloud AI/ML libraries including Google ADK, Vertex AI SDK, and common data science libraries (e.g., pandas, scikit-learn, TensorFlow/JAX). Experience with Google Cloud Platform services (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, Pub/Sub) and MLOps principles including Vertex AI Pipelines and CI/CD. Demonstrated success in building and deploying AI/ML models and solutions into production on cloud platforms. Demonstrated experience in a forward deployed role where you owned the business outcome, not just the ticket. Comfort operating in ambiguity. Job Overview The Vice President (VP) / Senior Software Engineer – Technical Remediation & Enablement Lead is a hands-on, code-level technical specialist responsible for driving the direct remediation of software vulnerabilities across enterprise application teams. This individual contributor / team-level technical lead works alongside application developers and contractor engineers to fix static code vulnerabilities (SAST), patch vulnerable software dependencies (SCA/third-party libraries), containerize workloads, and streamline local build/release pipelines to achieve same-day vulnerability hotfix and deployment capabilities. This role combines active software engineering (writing/refactoring code and debugging pipelines) with technical enablement, guiding squad developers on how to adopt internal security and build tools, resolve tricky dependency conflicts, and package applications into modern containers for rapid, low-risk production releases. Key Responsibilities & Core Duties 1. Hands-On Code Remediation & Dependency Patching Write, refactor, and review application code to directly remediate static code analysis (SAST) findings (e.g., SQL/command injection, cross-site scripting, insecure deserialization, improper error handling, weak cryptography). Resolve complex third-party library and framework upgrades (SCA/CVE remediation), managing transitive dependency conflicts, breaking API changes, and version incompatibilities across Java, Python, Go, .NET, or JavaScript/TypeScript stacks. Implement targeted automated unit, integration, and regression tests to validate that code fixes and patched libraries do not introduce functional regressions. 2. Containerization & Same-Day Release Enablement Work directly in application repositories to write and optimize Dockerfiles, container manifests, and base image configurations (Docker, OCI, Kubernetes/OpenShift). Assist application squads in containerizing non-containerized legacy services, establishing minimal base images and automated base-image rebuild triggers for same-day OS/runtime patching. Help configure and fine-tune CI/CD build scripts and release pipelines to compress deployment cycle times and eliminate manual deployment steps for emergency hotfixes. 3. Application Plan Technical Validation Perform code-level reviews of proposed remediation plans from application teams, verifying whether proposed library version bumps or refactored logic effectively eliminate the root cause of the vulnerability. Identify technical prerequisites (e.g., test coverage gaps, build tool upgrades, compiler/runtime updates) needed before a team can successfully patch and release. 4. Contractor Squad Pairing & PR Review Act as a peer reviewer and technical guide for external contractor engineers assigned to assist with remediation work. Review contractor-submitted pull requests (PRs) for code cleanliness, security correctness, test coverage, and enterprise architectural standards. Facilitate smooth technical onboarding and repository access for contractor developers. 5. Internal Tooling Adoption & Developer Feedback Actively pilot, adopt, and demonstrate internal developer tools, IDE security plugins, automated PR bots (e.g., Dependabot/Renovate patterns), and local scanning utilities within engineering squads. Troubleshoot false positives, scanner configuration errors, and build pipeline failures; provide direct, actionable feedback to internal platform and tooling teams to improve developer experience. Proven track record of directly fixing static code vulnerabilities (SAST) and managing third-party dependency/package upgrades in production environments. Practical, hands-on experience containerizing applications and working with container orchestration platforms (Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift). Technical Proficiencies Core Programming Languages: Strong, hands-on development proficiency in at least one or two primary enterprise languages: Java (Spring Boot), Python, Go, C#/.NET, or TypeScript/Node.js. Static Code Analysis (SAST): Ability to analyze and fix scanner findings from tools such as SonarQube, Checkmarx, Veracode, or Fortify. Dependency & Package Management: Practical experience with dependency resolution and build tools: Maven, Gradle, npm/yarn, NuGet, pip/Poetry, or Go modules, alongside SCA tools like Snyk, Black Duck, or JFrog Xray. Containers & Runtime: Hands-on experience creating production-grade Dockerfiles, managing multi-stage builds, patching container base images, and deploying to Kubernetes or OpenShift. CI/CD & Version Control: Proficient with Git, branching strategies (Gitflow/trunk-based), and pipeline configurations (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Tekton, GitLab CI, Harness). Developer-to-Developer Empathy Speaks the language of squad engineers, troubleshoots shoulder-to-shoulder, and offers practical solutions rather than abstract advice. Pragmatic Problem Solver Able to quickly find safe workarounds or code refactors when direct library upgrades introduce breaking API changes. TechGrove brings together India's deep pool of technical talent with Banyan's long-term approach to growth, creating a trusted, developer-focused environment where people can do their best work. About the role star/trac builds flow, a logistics platform for yards, gates and loading docks. It handles truck check-in, self- service terminals (kiosks), slot and dock planning, and real-time monitoring for industrial customers. We are moving flow from a single-tenant setup (WildFly, Oracle, one AWS account per customer, Elastic Beanstalk) to a cloud-native, multi-tenant platform: flow6, a multi-tenant flow API (Spring Boot, JDK 21) that serves many customers from one deployment, with strict tenant isolation flow-dynamic-ui, a configuration-driven frontend where pages, queries and forms are data, not code flow-terminal-service, the backend and configurator for our check-in kiosks An analytics and real-time layer: CDC from Postgres and Oracle into Apache Doris, Kafka (MSK), and live push to the UI much of our engineering runs through AI agents in Claude Code. Each agent has a written contract, hard rules and its own tools. Our infrastructure agents are DiVa, who works inside a workload account (EKS clusters, Dockerfiles, CI, GitOps deploys, image scans), and Otto, who works across the AWS Organization (accounts, SSO, shared networking, guardrails). They already do real work. They need a human principal who owns them. This role is that owner. You will run our platform end to end and set up what is still missing, with the agents doing much of the hands-on work under your direction. You will also keep making the agents better: safer, more capable, and more useful to the rest of the team. What you will do Own the platform Run our AWS estate: an AWS Organization with shared Networking, Monitoring and Shared Services accounts, plus customer workload accounts. EKS clusters (one per customer and environment, services as namespaces), ECR, RDS, MSK, Route 53. Own the deploy path end to end: GitLab CI from one standard template, then image build and scan, then a GitOps repo, then ArgoCD on EKS. Take new services to QA and then to production. Today that means flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, the auth service and Keycloak. Make flow6 safe to run as several pods behind one service: per-tenant Quartz schedulers, database locking, cache invalidation across pods, and health and readiness probes. Set up what is missing Production secrets: External Secrets Operator with SSM Parameter Store and pod-level IAM roles (IRSA / Pod Identity), in place of hand-made Kubernetes Secrets. Identity: Keycloak for staff, the existing auth service for customers, and service accounts for system-to- system calls. Observability across accounts with Grafana, Prometheus and Loki. Alarms that are tuned, not noisy. The data platform: Apache Doris, CDC pipelines (Postgres logical replication, Oracle LogMiner), Kafka. Repeatable customer onboarding: account, SSO, VPC, monitoring. Cost governance and a clear view of what runs where and what it costs. Lead the infrastructure agents Own DiVa's and Otto's contracts: their scope, hard rules, process steps and handoffs to the other agents. Turn repeated manual work into skills: small, deterministic Python tools with read-only doctor / list / plan verbs and gated mutating verbs. Examples are Helm releases, kubectl apply, registry cleanup, and an AWS Organization skill. Keep and strengthen the safety rails: agents never delete, every change needs an up-front confirm that states cost and blast radius, guard hooks block destructive commands, and nothing goes to main without review. Check that agent output is correct. Read what they produce, test it against real systems, and fix the contract when an agent is wrong. Record decisions as Target Architecture Decisions (TADs) and keep the shared memory accurate and sourced. Be the principal Make infrastructure decisions on your own and write them down so others can follow. Work with the architects, backend and frontend developers, QA, and our Cloud Ops lead, who runs the existing customer environments. Mentor colleagues who are new to Kubernetes or to working with agents. What you bring Senior to principal-level experience in DevOps, SRE or platform engineering, including running production systems. AWS in depth: EKS, IAM (including cross-account roles and SSO / Identity Center), VPC design (including shared VPCs, RAM, peering and endpoints), ECR, RDS, Secrets Manager / SSM. Kubernetes in production: Helm or Kustomize, GitOps with ArgoCD, add-ons, network setup, rolling deploys. CI/CD: GitLab CI preferred, including self-hosted runners. Container builds with multi-stage Dockerfiles, BuildKit and image scanning (Amazon Inspector). The JVM in containers: Spring Boot services, Gradle / Maven builds, Artifactory. Databases from an operator's view: Postgres and Oracle; connection pools, migrations (Liquibase), password rotation. Scripting: Python and Bash, written to be clear, repeatable and safe. Hands-on work with AI coding agents (Claude Code or similar), or a strong wish to start. You treat an agent as a capable colleague whose work you check, not as a black box. Safety by default: least privilege, no secrets in repos or images, confirm before you mutate, and an understanding of what an SCP or a delete can break. Clear written English. German is a strong plus: many of our customers and colleagues work in German. Nice to have Multi-tenant SaaS platforms: tenant isolation, per-tenant data sources, "no tenant, no service" designs. Kafka / MSK, Apache Doris or another OLAP engine, Debezium or other CDC tooling. Keycloak and OAuth2 / OIDC. Grafana, Prometheus and Loki across several AWS accounts. Moving legacy Java EE (WildFly) workloads to containers. Proxmox / LXC or other on-prem CI infrastructure. Writing prompts, agent contracts, or evaluation suites for LLM agents. Your first 90 days 1. Weeks 1–4: Learn the estate and the agents. Run DiVa and Otto on real tasks. Write down where their contracts are thin or wrong, and fix the first gaps. 2. Weeks 5–8: Finish the QA rollout of the new stack (flow6-mt, flow-dynamic-ui, auth service, Keycloak hardening). Put production secrets handling (ESO + SSM + IRSA) in place. 3. Weeks 9–12: Agree a production readiness plan for multi-pod flow6 and the first production cluster with the team. Ship at least one new DiVa skill that removes a manual step from that path. full_description: Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) – Platform Team (AWS + Hybrid) Purpose of Position We’re looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to join our Platform team and own the reliability of the systems that keep our company trading — from our AWS-based digital platform to the connectivity and point-of-sale systems in every store. One hour you’re tuning a Prometheus federation or an Open Telemetry pipeline; the next you’re troubleshooting a store’s connectivity at peak service. You’ll lead P0/P1 incident response, run blameless post-mortems, and build the observability and on-call practices that let a distributed, multi-site business run calmly through its busiest hours. Incident response: P0/P1 command, structured blameless post-mortems, and error-budget-driven release decisions. On-call by design: rosters built around operational peaks — breakfast, lunch, dinner, and weekend surge.
